description: The image displays a set of three pie charts, titled "easy," "medium," and "hard," which compare the proportions of four distinct categories across these three conditions. A shared legend is positioned to the right of the charts, identifying the four categories by color: N+K+ in teal, N−K+ in tan, N−K− in light orange, and N+K− in coral. Each chart contains four slices corresponding to these categories, with exact percentage labels displayed directly inside the respective slices. In the "easy" chart, the slices appear ordered clockwise by descending size, starting with the largest teal slice (N+K+) at 55.4%, followed by the tan slice (N−K+) at 38.3%, the light orange slice (N−K−) at 4.6%, and the coral slice (N+K−) at 1.7%. The "medium" chart follows a similar descending clockwise visual order, with the teal slice (N+K+) at 58.8%, the tan slice (N−K+) at 35.4%, the light orange slice (N−K−) at 4.0%, and the coral slice (N+K−) at 1.8%. In the "hard" chart, the proportions shift significantly, showing the light orange slice (N−K−) at 37.9%, the tan slice (N−K+) at 37.3%, the teal slice (N+K+) at 18.1%, and the coral slice (N+K−) at 6.7%. None of the slices in any of the three charts are visually emphasized through exploding, offsetting, or bolding.
